title: Travel Protection Plans: Underwriting Bulletin on the Evidence of a Prepaid Outlay
content:
The prepaid outlay standing against a journey insured by a Travel Protection Plans certificate is read from the vacation package the cover was bought alongside, one of the Vacation Package Products: the lines posted to that package's ledger, the standing of the package, and the amount the package records as paid.

Where the package's ledger carries a line settling the balance of the package and the package stands confirmed, travelling, completed or cancelled, the prepaid outlay is taken as every line posted to the package under its routine terms less the agency service fee charged on it.

Where the package's ledger carries no line settling the balance and the package stands confirmed, travelling, completed or cancelled, the prepaid outlay is taken as the amount the package records as paid.

Where neither holds, the prepaid outlay is taken as the package's quoted price.

## The three readings

| Line settling the balance on the package's ledger | Standing of the package | The prepaid outlay is taken as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At least 1 stands | Confirmed, travelling, completed or cancelled | Every line posted to the package under its routine terms, less the agency service fee charged on it |
| None stands | Confirmed, travelling, completed or cancelled | The amount the package records as paid |
| Either way | Any other standing | The package's quoted price |

## Reading the package

Both of the first two readings require the package to stand in one of those four states; they are told apart by whether a line settling the balance of the package has been posted to its ledger. Where the balance has been settled, the ledger itself is the measure, and every line posted under the package's routine terms is counted, less the agency service fee charged on it. Where it has not, the ledger is not the measure and the amount the package records as paid is taken instead.

Where the package stands in none of those four states, neither of the first two readings is reached whatever its ledger carries, and the package's quoted price is taken.

Hypothetically, on a package standing as completed whose ledger carries a line settling the balance, with routine lines of 6800.00 USD and an agency service fee of 120.00 USD among them, the prepaid outlay is 6680.00 USD. On the same package with no line settling the balance, the prepaid outlay is whatever the package records as paid, which might be 3400.00 USD where only a deposit has gone through.
